title: dedicated-autoscaler-smoother-burst-control-and-util-reporting
author: Priya Nair
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets experience occasional sharp drops in throughput when tenants consume short-lived bursts; current token-bucket burst controls are too aggressive in some workload patterns and the utilization reporting is noisy, making it hard for SRE and customers to understand headroom. This PR smooths burst consumption across short timescales, fixes a race in the token refill path, and improves fleet-level utilization reporting to reflect effective capacity after burst allocation.

What I changed: - Implemented a leaky-bucket smoothing layer on top of the existing token-bucket to spread short burst drains over a configurable smoothing window (default 15s). - Fixed race where token refill worker could double-count tokens during leader failover by introducing a compare-and-swap refill marker. - Added per-fleet effective_capacity and burst_utilization metrics exported to Prometheus (redwood.autoscaler.fleet_effective_capacity, redwood.autoscaler.fleet_burst_utilization). - Adjusted autoscaler decision logic to use effective_capacity when evaluating scale-up/scale-down thresholds so transient bursts don't trigger oscillation. - Added integration tests that simulate leader failover + burst storms and an end-to-end e2e that validates metric shapes over time. - Updated docs and release notes.

Why: This reduces observed oscillations where Dedicated fleets would scale up for bursts then immediately scale down, causing customer latency spikes and excess cost. The metrics changes give operators a clearer view of how much capacity is reserved/available for steady traffic versus bursts.

Testing: - Unit tests for token-bucket + leaky smoothing layer. - New integration test harness scenario 'burst-storm-leader-failover' added to perf-canary. - Ran full CI (build/test/lint) and a 24-hour soak on a staging dedicated fleet (n=12 GPUs) with synthetic bursty traffic. Metrics show a 38% reduction in scale oscillation events and stable p95 latency under load.

Migration/rollout: - Feature guarded behind runtime flag `autoscaler.enable_smoothing_v2` disabled by default. - Gradual rollout plan: enable for 10% of fleets for 24h, monitor redwood.autoscaler.scale_events, then ramp to 100% if stable.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics exported - [x] Docs updated - [x] Release notes included

Release notes: Smoother burst controls for Dedicated fleets to reduce scale oscillations and new fleet-level metrics (redwood.autoscaler.fleet_effective_capacity, redwood.autoscaler.fleet_burst_utilization). Feature is behind a runtime flag and rolled out gradually.

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Could you clarify why the 15s default was chosen? Is it derived from observed workload traces?
Priya Nair: The 15s window is conservative based on 30-day trace percentile analysis (median burst duration ~7s, 95th < 40s). We expose it as a runtime parameter for tuning per-customer.
Lena Chen: The atomic refill marker looks good, but please add a comment explaining the leader-failover sequence; I had trouble following it initially.
Priya Nair: Added detailed comments and a unit test that exercises leader handoff paths.
Marco Alvarez: CI flake on the new e2e - timing-dependent. Suggest using a retry/backoff in test harness; otherwise LGTM.
Priya Nair: Updated test harness with deterministic clocks and a retry; reran CI.
Evan Brooks: Approving after test fixes - observed lower oscillation rate in staging metrics. Approve.
ci_summary: Initial CI: failed (flaky e2e timing). Rerun after deterministic clock fix: all checks passed (build/test/lint/bench).
notes_for_ops: Rollout behind runtime flag autoscaler.enable_smoothing_v2. Recommend enabling on 10% fleets for 24h, monitor redwood.autoscaler.scale_events and redwood.autoscaler.fleet_burst_utilization. If scale_events spike by >10% or p95 latency increases >5% roll back the flag.
release_notes: Smoother burst controls for Dedicated fleets: adds a leaky-bucket smoothing layer to the token-bucket burst control, fixes refill race on leader failover, and exports fleet-level effective_capacity and burst_utilization metrics. Rollout behind runtime flag and gradual ramp recommended.
